title: One Point Lesson - Reflux Pump Low-Level Protection (LSLL-8901) (OPL-FA-8901-05)
content:
ONE POINT LESSON (OPL): OPL-FA-8901-05 - Reflux Pump Low-Level Protection (LSLL-8901).

Equipment: FA-8901 (REFLUX ACCUMULATOR DRUM), Discipline: Instrument, Area: 8900 - HEXANE COLUMN OVERHEAD SYSTEM.

Related Interlock: SEQ-8901 (SIL 1), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-8901.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
This One Point Lesson explains reflux pump low-level protection (lsll-8901) for FA-8901 (REFLUX ACCUMULATOR DRUM) in the HEXANE COLUMN OVERHEAD SYSTEM. A low drum level cavitates and damages the GA-8920 reflux pump; the LSLL trip must be proven and never casually bypassed. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:
- Precaution 1: De-energise and isolate the loop; place the function to bypass/inhibit under permit.
- Precaution 2: Inform the panel operator before working on any trip, valve or transmitter.
- Precaution 3: Take care with instrument air / hydraulic pressure when disconnecting tubing.
- Precaution 4: Verify intrinsic-safety / Ex integrity is restored before returning to service.
- Precaution 5: Wear correct PPE and follow ESD/override control procedures.

TOOLS & MATERIALS:
- Tool 1: HART communicator / positioner software (e.g. ValveLink)
- Tool 2: Loop calibrator & decade box / pressure source
- Tool 3: Digital multimeter and clamp meter
- Tool 4: Span/zero test gas or reference standards
- Tool 5: Torque screwdriver and small hand tools
- Tool 6: Certified test/inhibit permit

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 - Action: Confirm the LSLL-8901 trip stops GA-8920
- Step 1 - Check: Loop isolated / under permit
- Step 2 - Action: Test the trip during commissioning and proof tests
- Step 2 - Check: Reference standard traceable
- Step 3 - Action: Never bypass the trip without an authorised permit
- Step 3 - Check: As-found & as-left recorded
- Step 4 - Action: Investigate any repeated low-level events
- Step 4 - Check: Trip / control action verified
- Step 5 - Action: Verify the pump restarts only after level recovers
- Step 5 - Check: Return to service confirmed

COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING:
- Symptom: Reflux drum level transmitter drifting vs gauge | Likely Cause: Transmitter zero drift | Action: Recalibrated LT-8901 against the bridle gauge
- Symptom: Blanket / vent split-range valve hunting | Likely Cause: Split-range calibration overlap incorrect | Action: Re-tuned PCV-8905 split-range, verified PT-8902 hold
- Symptom: Proof test of drum high-high level trip | Likely Cause: Within tolerance | Action: Recalibrated LSHH-8901 and verified EFF-1 column feed trip

KEY LEARNING POINTS:
- Point 1: A low drum level cavitates and damages the GA-8920 reflux pump; the LSLL trip must be proven and never casually bypassed.
- Point 2: Respect the interlock SEQ-8901: e.g. LSHH-8901 trips at > 85 % - never defeat it without a permit.
- Point 3: Always cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID TJC-LLD-PID-8901 before working on FA-8901.
- Point 4: Record the work in the equipment history so the Knowledge Hub stays the single source of truth.
